pageCache.pageTitle: Hart Plain Junior School - Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
At Hart Plain, we believe passionately in the importance of inclusion and equality for all children, in all aspects of school life. We strive to ensure our core values of aspiration, courage, integrity, happiness and respect are at the heart of our SEND provision.
We pride ourselves on the strong collaborations and positive relationships amongst pupils, parents, carers and staff that we have established. We actively promote a policy of openness and accessibility to encourage these partnerships. We will always involve parents and children throughout their journey with us and this collective ethos underpins our SEND philosophy.
We know that the earlier we identify SEND and provide support, the more successful our children will be. As such, we foster a personal and bespoke approach to identifying and providing for, the individual needs of children with SEND.
School staff, at all levels, have the knowledge and skills to support all children, including those with SEND. Senior leaders take collective responsibility for establishing effective SEND provision and championing the needs of the children throughout the curriculum. We also work closely with outside agencies to offer encompassing support, advice and expertise.
We actively promote independent working for all our children and we understand the particular importance of ensuring children with SEND are able to access learning that is specifically tailored to suit their needs. We are committed to providing highly skilled, professional support and resources for children with SEND to enable them to fulfil their individual potential and achieve their next steps in education.
Please read our SEND Information Report document as this answers any questions that you may have about how your child's learning, physical or emotional needs are supported by staff at Hart Plain Junior School. It tells you who to talk to and what support is in place to support your child. This document is located at the bottom of this page. Please also read our SEND Policy for additional information. If you would like to request an enlarged print version of any document or you would like it read to you, please email the school office at adminoffice@hartplain-jun.hants.sch.uk.
Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCO) is Heidi Connolly. Please make an appointment with your child's class teacher or with Mrs Connolly if you have any concerns about your child's progress. Contact: Heidi Connolly
adminoffice@hartplain-jun.hants.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Hart Plain Junior School - SEND RESOURCES
pageCache.text:
SEND RESOURCES
On this page you will find a collection of information, website links, tips and resources to help you support your children with their additional needs, learning and self-esteem.
Children have varying needs and there is no single approach that will suit everyone. It is quite common for children to have additional needs that span all these areas, so select the resources that meet the needs of your child, without worrying too much about the label or category they fall under. Everyone has strengths and weaknesses and these SEND strategies will be beneficial to many children, whether or not they have a diagnosis.
Guidance on SEND resources for home education from the Department for Education:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/coronavirus-covid-19-online-education-resources/online-science-pe-wellbeing-and-send-resources-for-home-education

pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values at Hart Plain Junior School
Respect is a strong part of Hart Plain Junior School and is part of its core Values. Pupils learn that their behaviours has an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect and this is reiterated through the schools teaching and learning environments.

Admissions Information
If you’re considering our school for your child, we’d love to welcome you!
We encourage families to visit our school. If you would like to discover more about our school, please give us a call and we’ll arrange a tour of the school at a time that works for you – or explore our website for a virtual look at our school life.
For full details on admissions, including our policies and in-year application process, please visit our Admissions Arrangements page. If you are looking for more information about our Year 3 places, please visit our New Year 3 Intake page.

Wraparound Care

Curriculum
A Lifetime Love of Learning
We aim to provide children with a broad and balanced curriculum in order to achieve our vision and develop an understanding of our core values:
At Hart Plain Junior School we foster a lifetime love of learning, where children acquire the knowledge, skills, resilience and heart to pursue and achieve their individual dreams.
Integrity - We do the right thing and make responsible choices even when it is difficult
Happiness - We know what makes us happier and how to make our community a better place for all
Aspiration - We strive to succeed and to be the very best we can in order to achieve our goals
Respect - We treat others as we would like them to treat us and celebrate our differences
Courage - We have the bravery to tackle the challenges of life and face them head on
Each year group has their own page dedicated to the curriculum covered within the academic year.
Trips and experiences play a crucial role in broadening pupils' knowledge and understanding at Key Stage 2 by providing them with real-world contexts that enhance their learning. Below is a list of our current planned activities for this academic year.
At Hart Plain Junior we recognise the importance of all aspects of safeguarding within the teaching and experiences we offer. A copy of our safeguarding curriculum is also located below.
Our music development plan is also available to view below.
Parents in England have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE) at Key Stage 2. This applies to all types of schools, including academies and free schools. Parents don’t need to give a reason, and the school must respect their decision. While the school must supervise the child during RE lessons, it doesn’t have to provide extra teaching or activities during that time.
Remote education delivery, if required, would be in line with the government guidance which is located here. In order to deliver this, we would use a combination of Purple Mash and Oak National Academy work. Details would be communicated via Arbor to all parents and carers.
If you require any further information regarding the school curriculum, please email the school office.
